clue.text: Man, for example, accepted by theologian as the pattern

indicators.note: something accepted by another is taken in, so the second piece goes inside the theologian's name

parts.note: William Paley was an English theologian, author of Natural Theology
the Isle of Man is an island, abbreviated Is.

explanation.surface: A Manxman is welcomed by a churchman as a model to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person but is the Isle of Man; Is. is the standard abbreviation for island, set inside PALEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Paisley is a fabric design of curved teardrop shapes, a kind of decorative motif.

clue.text: Creatures much put upon take slippers in case

parts.note: to pack is to put into a case, as for a journey
mules are backless slippers

explanation.surface: Bring your slippers in your suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take ... in case' reads as luggage; PACK is to put in a case, and MULES are backless slippers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pack mules are beasts of burden, loaded with heavy loads.

clue.text: Like a party under cover?

parts.note: a party under cover suggests a hidden gathering or spy, but means a person protected by an insurance policy

explanation.surface: A secret celebration held indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' is the legal sense, a person to a contract; 'cover' is insurance protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with a policy has cover against loss, so is protected financially.

clue.text: Left with repairs to Noah's vessel, found usurer

indicators.note: repairs to suggests the letters of the word are fixed up into a new order

parts.note: Noah's gives its letters NOAHS
an ark is a vessel, as Noah's was

explanation.surface: A workman left after mending the Ark and met a moneylender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repairs to' looks like a visit to the vessel; it signals rearranging the patriarch's name, and 'found' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A loan shark lends money at extortionate interest, a predatory lender.

clue.text: Way of thinking about an attempt on fourth of July

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the following pieces below the first
fourth of picks out the fourth letter of the word July
about means turned around, so the pair of words reads backwards

parts.note: a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: Considering a try at something on Independence Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns A GO into OGA, placed under Y. 'fourth of July' looks like the US holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoga is a Hindu discipline of meditation and philosophy, a mental and spiritual system.

clue.text: Initially Carmen' has divine voice but little craft

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter of the word Carmen

parts.note: an oracle is a voice through which a god speaks

explanation.surface: The opera's heroine sings like a goddess, though she has no great skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' reads as skill in the surface, but here it means a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A coracle is a small round wicker boat, a tiny vessel.

clue.text: These turbulent priests could have corns by tea-break!

indicators.note: could have signals the priests' name is formed from these letters rearranged

parts.note: only the tea part of tea-break enters the mix, the break hinting at the scrambling

explanation.surface: Wild clerics might get foot trouble from their afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: CORNS BY TEA gives the ten letters; the exclamation mark flags the playful image.
explanation.definitionFit: The Corybantes were frenzied priests of the goddess Cybele, known for wild dancing.

clue.text: Teacher's pet practically

indicators.note: practically means almost all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a rabbit is a common pet

explanation.surface: The teacher's favourite pupil, almost literally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teacher's pet' looks like a favourite pupil; 'pet' is a rabbit, cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher; the word means my master.

clue.text: Sculptor nominally welcome in Florence?

parts.note: the artist's first name, Benvenuto, is Italian for welcome, and he was a Florentine

explanation.surface: An artist who would be well received in Florence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nominally' points to the first name, not to a polite reception.
explanation.definitionFit: Benvenuto Cellini was a Florentine Renaissance goldsmith and sculptor of Perseus.

clue.text: Priest with a name for being a lover of lamb, we hear

parts.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A cleric known for his fondness for roast lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb wrote as Elia; an admirer of his essays is called by this adjective. 'we hear' says lamb is the author Lamb, not mutton.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a devotee of Charles Lamb's Essays of Elia.

clue.text: Conspirator responsible for the highest rent?

definitions.text: Conspirator responsible for the highest rent?

parts.words: Conspirator responsible for the highest rent?
parts.note: rent reads as money paid to a landlord, but means a tear: Antony in Julius Caesar says 'See what a rent the envious ... made' in Caesar's cloak

explanation.surface: Which plotter charged tenants the most?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests property rent; Shakespeare's line uses rent as a gash, and this plotter struck the first blow.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the assassins of Julius Caesar, who made a famous tear in his mantle.

clue.text: Happy in France to devour coarse biscuit

indicators.note: to devour is to swallow up, so the coarse word is taken inside the French word

parts.note: gai is French for happy
ribald means coarse or vulgar

explanation.surface: A cheerful French person wolfs down a rough cracker.
explanation.walkthrough: GA + RIBALD + I. A Garibaldi is a British biscuit with a layer of squashed currants.
explanation.definitionFit: A Garibaldi is a currant-filled British cookie named after the Italian patriot.

clue.text: Gunners trapped in boggy ground or marsh

indicators.note: trapped in means held inside, so the gunners go within the boggy ground

parts.note: a moss is a peat bog in Scotland and northern England
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

explanation.surface: Artillerymen get stuck in a swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: Moss in the sense of a peat bog is a northern British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is a bog or swamp, wet ground that is hard to cross.

clue.text: Blank state produced by "Russian Flower violin arrangement

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ob is a great Russian river

indicators.note: an arrangement of a piece puts its notes, here the letters of violin, in a new order

explanation.surface: A tune called Russian Flower, arranged for violin, leaves the listener in a trance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the crossword river (something that flows), not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblivion is the condition of being unaware or forgotten, a mental void.

clue.text: Regular tunnel not found in Winchester?

definitions.text: Regular tunnel not found in Winchester?

parts.words: Regular tunnel not found in Winchester?
parts.note: tunnel and Winchester suggest a city, but a Winchester rifle has a grooved barrel, unlike a plain uniform one

explanation.surface: An ordinary underpass that the cathedral city lacks.
explanation.walkthrough: Winchester is a city in Hampshire, England, but also the American rifle.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoothbore gun has a barrel without rifling grooves.

clue.text: Changed daily woman

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of daily are put in a different order

explanation.surface: The charwoman has been replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is British slang for a cleaning lady, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydia is a female first name, so it stands for a lady.

clue.text: Chap eating out needs some salt

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of eating are disordered

explanation.surface: A man who dines out wants a bit of seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating out' looks like dining in a restaurant; 'out' is the anagram signal on EATING.
explanation.definitionFit: Manganite is a manganese mineral, and also the name for a salt of manganous acid.

clue.text: Letting oneself down? It can be seen on the face

definitions.text: Letting oneself down? It can be seen on the face

parts.words: Letting oneself down? It can be seen on the face
parts.note: letting oneself down suggests shame showing on one's face, but means descending a rock face on a rope

explanation.surface: Disappointment in yourself shows in your expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face' is a cliff face, not a human face.
explanation.definitionFit: Abseiling is descending a cliff by rope, controlling the drop.

clue.text: Trojan hero's endless curse from outer part of cell

indicators.note: endless means the Trojan's name loses both its first and last letters

parts.note: Hector was the greatest Trojan warrior in the Iliad
blast is a mild curse

explanation.surface: A Trojan warrior swears constantly about a prison wall.
explanation.walkthrough: HECTOR without its first and last letters gives ECTO. 'cell' reads as a prison room, but is a biological cell.
explanation.definitionFit: The ectoblast is the outer membrane of a cell, also an embryo's outer layer.

clue.text: Wild pigeon race plummeted in America

parts.note: stock means race or lineage
Americans use dove as the past tense of dive

explanation.surface: A bird's ancestry crashed in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: British English says 'dived'; the American past tense supplies the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock dove is a European pigeon that nests in tree holes.

clue.text: A month to work as an ink-slinger

parts.note: Oct. is October, a month
an opus is a work, especially of music

explanation.surface: A writer gives a month to working on a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ink-slinger' looks like a hack writer; it is a creature that squirts ink.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus squirts ink to escape predators.

clue.text: Vision is feeble — line has dis. appeared

indicators.note: has disappeared (split across a line break on the page) means the line letter goes missing from the word

parts.note: slight means feeble or weak

explanation.surface: Someone's eyesight is weak, and a line of text has vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: The page splits 'disappeared' over a line break, which the text renders as 'dis. appeared'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is the faculty of seeing, the power of the eyes.

clue.text: Senior lady piano-scholar

parts.note: a grand is a kind of piano
MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar's degree

explanation.surface: An elderly woman who is both pianist and academic.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandmother is an older woman of the family, a grandparent.

clue.text: Playing an hautboy endlessly, the German way

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with, so they are rearranged
endlessly means the word hautboy loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone performs on an old oboe without stopping, as Germans do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the Y from HAUTBOY (an old name for an oboe), leaving HAUTBO; 'Playing' shuffles AN with it. 'endlessly' looks like 'without stopping'.
explanation.definitionFit: An Autobahn is a motorway in Germany, the German word for an express highway.

clue.text: Stop at sea

parts.note: the clue gives the sailor's command meaning halt

explanation.definitionFit: Avast is a nautical order to cease or hold.

clue.text: House wine receptacle to disappear

parts.note: a bin is a rack or case for storing wine
to go is to disappear or vanish

explanation.surface: A cheap wine stored in the cellar vanishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House wine' reads as cheap restaurant wine; 'House' is the game, also called housey-housey in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: House is the old British name for the numbers game played with called numbers and cards.

clue.text: Raising agent to make pointed remark about Olympic finalists

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the pointed remark goes round the final letters

parts.note: a barb is a cutting or pointed remark
the last two letters of Olympic are I and C

explanation.surface: A coach needles athletes who reached the Olympic final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finalists' looks like athletes but means the closing letters of 'Olympic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bicarb, short for bicarbonate of soda, makes cakes rise in baking.

clue.text: Bite crisp biscuit

definitions.meaning: to bite is to snatch at with the teeth
a brandy or ginger biscuit with a crunch

explanation.definitionFit: A dog bites with a sudden snatch of its jaws, and a gingernut-like cookie shares the name.

clue.text: Instrument for long-distance offpeak calls

parts.note: off-peak calls sounds like cheap phone rates, but means calls sent out from a mountain peak across valleys

explanation.surface: A telephone for cheap long-distance calls in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: Off-peak is a phone tariff; here it is literally off a peak, the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpenhorn is a very long wooden horn used by Swiss herdsmen to signal over mountains.

clue.text: Boxed jewel at end of a passage?

definitions.meaning: The Jewel in the Crown was a TV series on the box set in the Raj, the country being the jewel in Britain's crown
E. M. Forster's novel A Passage to ... ends with this country's name

explanation.surface: A gem in a case at the end of a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxed' means shown on TV ('the box'); 'passage' is Forster's novel, not a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: The subcontinent was called the jewel in the crown of the Empire, and it closes the title of Forster's novel.

clue.text: Trousers, perhaps, not right in this silk

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged otherwise
not means the right letter is left out of trousers

explanation.surface: Trousers might well be made of this fabric, though not the correct kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops one R from TROUSERS, leaving TOUSERS, which 'perhaps' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Tussore is a coarse wild silk from India, also spelt tussah.

clue.text: Colourful display of buttons by worker

parts.note: buttons is old slang for a pageboy, from the buttons on his uniform
a worker is an ant, the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A show of coloured buttons put on by a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buttons' looks like fasteners; it is a pageboy (a hotel or house servant boy in a buttoned uniform).
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a spectacular parade or procession in costume.
